conviction_note: abs_move 7.0 (the name's median reaction of 6.98, kept whole because a first FY27 guide plus Burpee and TRIXIE commentary lands with this print) times a mild 55 p_up lean from a low implied Q4 bar and Scotts' above-consensus FY27 garden guide. The lean is offset by deal and data costs and soft pet peers, and the bar is disputed between sources; findings sum to +0.5, close to the scaled +0.7.
bar: Q4 FY26: Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-18) puts consensus at -$0.06 non-GAAP EPS on ~$600.2M revenue (https://finviz.com/news/424819/central-garden-pets-seasonal-low-quarter-sets-the-stage-for-its-fiscal-2027-outlook). The same piece gives FY26 consensus at $2.89, which against reported YTD non-GAAP EPS of $3.04 (Q1 $0.21, Q2 $1.29, Q3 $1.54) implies Q4 near -$0.15. A Zacks snippet cites FY26 consensus of $3.00 (implied Q4 near -$0.04). The company guide is FY26 '$2.85 or better' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000887733/000088773326000019/q32026pressrelease.htm), which implies Q4 of -$0.19 or better. The estimate sources disagree, so every bar-dependent finding is capped small. No sourced FY27 consensus exists beyond one Zacks firm estimate of $2.93, which is likely stale.
positioning_check: No usable option chain (baseline options status no_paired_strikes), so there is no skew. Latest short interest found: 379.0K CENT shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement, 3.0 days to cover (FINRA via curvedtrading.com, search snippet only; the page returned 403 on fetch). Against ~9.65M CENT common shares outstanding that is about 4%: not crowded. The main float is CENTA, which was not separately found. Spot $46.78 is 3.8% under the 52-week high and 48.8% over the low; run-up is +3.3% over 20 days and flat over 5 days. 7 of the last 8 prints moved up.

findings.finding: Reported YTD FY26 non-GAAP EPS is $3.04 (Q1 $0.21, Q2 $1.29, Q3 $1.54) against a full-year guide of '$2.85 or better', so the guide only requires a Q4 of -$0.19 or better. Last year's Q4 was -$0.09, and Earnings Whispers' Q4 consensus is -$0.06. The guide floor is far below even the weakest consensus reading, the pattern this company has used before (FY25 delivered $2.73 against an initial '$2.20 or better'-style floor).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 (2025-11-24): a narrower-than-expected Q4 loss of -$0.09 plus a flat FY26 guide bought +8.65%. CENT is up on 7 of its last 8 prints (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus at -$0.06 already sits above the guide-implied -$0.19. If the Street were fully there, the FY26 consensus would read about $3.00 everywhere, yet one widely carried preview still shows $2.89. Capped because the bar is disputed.
findings.independence: Q1 and Q2 figures come from separate releases: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/887733/000088773326000004/q12026pressrelease.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000887733/000088773326000011/q22026pressrelease.htm

findings.finding: Scotts Miracle-Gro, the closest garden peer, reported on 2026-11-04, after CENT last spoke. It guided FY27 adjusted EPS to $4.70-4.90 with 2-4% sales growth, above estimates, and the stock rose about 8.7%. It noted the lawn and garden category grew 5%+ in 2026, with roughly 4% gross pricing planned. Against that, retailer inventories are up low single digits and SMG flagged about $100M of commodity and freight inflation. Garden was 55% of CENT's Q3 sales ($482M of $882M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CENT's Garden segment drove Q3 (sales +3%, GAAP operating income +9%); FY guide raise at Q3 bought +5.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: CENT is +3.3% over 20 days, which covers the SMG print. CENT's garden mix (wild bird, grass seed, controls, live plants) differs from SMG's branded fertilizer, and on the Q3 call CENT said its garden retailer inventories were negative net of the new fertilizer distribution. That is a cleaner position than SMG's inventory build. Sized net of the 45% pet half, which F3 covers.
findings.independence: SMG release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000825542/000082554226000061/exhibit991q4f26newsrelease.htm (the same company, so not independent of the article). Separately, CENT's Q3 call (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/central-garden-pet-co/earnings/2026-q3) said garden retailer inventories were in good position.

findings.finding: Pet peers since CENT last spoke are soft. Spectrum Brands (2026-11-12) cited Global Pet Care Q4 sales declines on aquatics softness (FY organic about -1.1%, aquatics down low double digits; CENT also sells aquatics) and guided FY27 flat to low single digits. Tractor Supply cited continued new-pet-acquisition headwinds. CENT's own Q3 call reported super-premium trade-down and a channel shift to club and Walmart. Pet was 45% of CENT's Q3 sales and is shrinking on the distribution exit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: Pet sales -19% reported (+2% organic), with a supplier plant fire hitting Dog & Cat; stock still +5.63% on the EPS raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy evidence. If the soft pet read were priced, CENT would not sit 3.8% from its 52-week high. Freshpet (+10% sales) and Nestle Petcare (+5.3% organic) show consumables holding, so the weakness is in durables and aquatics, which is CENT's mix.
findings.independence: Tractor Supply pet commentary: https://globalpetindustry.com/news/tractor-supplys-pet-business-grows-5-in-q3-as-sales-trends-improve/ . Opposite direction: Freshpet https://www.petfoodprocessing.net/articles/21055-freshpet-grows-q3-sales-10-posts-strongest-adjusted-gross-margin-in-seven-years

findings.finding: CENT acquired W. Atlee Burpee (packet seed and young plants) in a deal that closed 2026-09-30, day one of FY27. It was announced 2026-10-19 with terms and sales undisclosed, and the company said details would come on the Q4 call. The deal adds an unquantified contribution to the first FY27 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print reacted to a CENT bolt-on disclosure in the baseline; the TRIXIE announcement (2026-07-27) preceded a +5.63% Q3 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: With no price or revenue disclosed, no estimate can include it. If it were priced, FY27 estimates would have moved after 2026-10-19, and no revision was found.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call the CFO said higher corporate spending on TRIXIE and data capabilities accounted for more than 100% of the non-GAAP operating income decline. He also said not to expect TRIXIE synergies until the second year. TRIXIE (80% for EUR 340M plus up to EUR 60M earn-out) is still pending, with close expected in H1 FY27. So the first FY27 guide probably carries deal and data costs, may exclude TRIXIE, and comes in the company's habitual conservative 'or better' form. The FY26 initial guide was $2.70 'or better' against FY25 actual of $2.73.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last first-guide print (2025-11-24) issued a flat 'or better' guide and still bought +8.65%, so the conservative style has not been punished. That is why this finding is small.
findings.why_not_priced: FY27 consensus is not sourced (one Zacks estimate of $2.93, likely stale). If the market expected a near-flat guide off a ~$3.00 FY26 base, the stock would not sit near its 52-week high. Capped because the FY27 bar is unsourced.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview flags deal costs and data investments as an ongoing drag: https://finviz.com/news/424819/central-garden-pets-seasonal-low-quarter-sets-the-stage-for-its-fiscal-2027-outlook

findings.finding: IEEPA tariff refunds are possible. CENT recognized $3.6M of refunds in Pet in Q3, excluded them from non-GAAP, and its FY26 guide excludes additional refunds. Spectrum Brands booked $57.4M of net IEEPA refunds in FY26, so CENT may book a further GAAP-only refund in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 refund was excluded from non-GAAP and did not register in the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Below the non-GAAP line and outside the guide; it has no path to the FY27 guide, so it is sized at a fraction.

findings.finding: Fertilizer input costs have eased. Middle East granular urea is about $425/t for November delivery (US Gulf about $424/st), down from a $782 wartime peak and near or below the pre-war $455-470 range. That eases the FY27 fertilizer cost and pricing pressure the preview flagged for CENT's Garden segment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CENT reaction on input-cost guidance found.
findings.source_date: 2026-11 (search summary; November 6, 2026 paper-market report quoted second-hand)
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed. SMG had locked over 80% of its urea at higher levels, and CENT may have done the same, so the relief may not reach FY27.

findings.finding: Planned Garden leadership change: J.D. Walker (President, Garden Consumer Products) retired 2026-09-26 and was succeeded internally by Jason Barnes. Management framed it as planned.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced two months ago and internal; it is in the price and only matters if the call ties it to the FY27 garden plan.

findings.finding: Positioning leaves little cushion. The stock is 3.8% under its 52-week high, 48.8% above its low and up on 7 of its last 8 prints, while short interest is modest (about 379K CENT shares, 3.0 days to cover, August 2026). There is no squeeze fuel, and an upbeat reaction appears to be the market's expectation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The single down print in 8 (2025-08-06, -10.96%) came off a strong run.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; filed small as context on how the reaction function may be skewed.
